title: On‑Prem GitOps + Helm Upgrade Playbook (ArgoCD + Image Signing)
content:
Status: draft

Purpose
This is a working playbook for CI/CD and release mechanics tailored to Redwood private deployments (VPC / on‑prem). It focuses on an ArgoCD GitOps control plane + Helm chart model with mandatory image signing (cosign), Terraform modules for infra, and practical upgrade/rollback procedures. Aim: reduce blast radius of upgrades and make private upgrade runbooks repeatable across customer environments.

Scope and Audience
- Audience: solutions engineers, SREs, deployment engineers, and customer ops teams.
- Scope: cluster-level GitOps patterns (ArgoCD), Helm packaging conventions, image signing & verification, Terraform module notes for network/registry access, upgrade strategies (canary/blue-green/straight), and hands‑on rollback/incident guidance.
- Out of scope: packaging model artifacts, hosted API release cadence, licensing/legal review steps.

High-Level Architecture Pattern
- Source-of-truth: deployment repo (git) per customer containing values files, ArgoCD Application definitions (app-of-apps).
- ArgoCD (control plane) runs in the customer cluster (or in customer VPC) with restricted RBAC and read-only access to production branches.
- Helm charts: stable chart repo mirrored into customer‑scoped chart registry. Charts are parameterized via values/* and sealed via a policy review.
- OCI images: built by CI, signed with cosign, uploaded to customer-permitted registry. ArgoCD sync only allowed for signed images.
- Terraform: manages VPC networks, private ECR/harbor integration, service accounts, and ArgoCD bootstrap IAM objects.

Prereqs and Assumptions
- Customer cluster reachable from CI runner (or runners run in customer's VPN).
- A container registry that supports image signing verification (Harbor with cosign or ECR + cosign verifier).
- ArgoCD version >= 2.6 (for app-of-apps and OCI image detector hooks).
- Terraform state stored in a customer-appropriate backend (S3/GCS/on-prem equivalent).
- KMS/HSM accessible for cosign key management (or cosign key stored in secure vault).

Terraform Module Notes (quick reference)
- Modules referenced here are opinionated and intentionally small: vpc-net, registry-integration, argocd-bootstrap, cluster-roles.
- vpc-net: outputs subnets, nat gateways, private route tables. Keep tags stable (redwood:customer-id).
- registry-integration: sets up IAM role/service-account for CI to push images, creates registry policies to allow signature verification.
- argocd-bootstrap: creates namespace argocd, service account, OIDC config if needed, and initial AppProject for customer apps.
- recommended usage: pin module versions in customer repo; do not use latest for bootstrap in production without a canary run.

CI Build & Image Signing (recommended flow)
1. CI builds image -> runs unit/integration tests -> calculates SBOM (optional) -> cosign sign (private key stored in vault) -> push to customer registry with signature.
2. CI creates a release tag and updates the kustomize/helm values file in the customer deployment repo via an automated PR. PR must attach digest and signed artifact metadata.
3. Release PR triggers an image verification job that validates cosign signature against the customer's public verification key.

Image Signing Practicals
- Tooling: cosign (1.15+ recommended). Use OCI digest pins in Helm values (image: repo/name@sha256:...).
- Key management: prefer KMS-backed keys; rotate yearly or on compromise. Keep a signing key per org/customer.
- Verifier: ArgoCD requires an admission/argocd-image-updater plugin or an image-policy-webhook that rejects unsigned images.
- Fallback: if verifier is down, policy must specify whether sync is blocked or allowed with elevated approvals.

ArgoCD + Helm: App-of-Apps Pattern
- Top-level repo contains a single argocd-apps.yaml (app-of-apps) which references child Application objects (customer-app, infra-app, monitoring-app).
- Each child app points to a specific path and revision (prefer tags or pinned commits).
- Values files: store values/<env>/<component>.yaml in the same repo; limit secrets to sealed-secrets/vault references.
- Helm charts: store chart references as OCI or chartmuseum URLs. Prefer OCI chart references with digest pins.

Upgrade Strategies
- Canary (recommended for stateful or high-risk components): deploy new version to small subset of nodes/replicas using HelmRelease or Argo Rollouts, observe metrics (latency, error rates, token throughput), then promote.
- Blue/Green: create parallel deployment (green) with new chart values and route a % of traffic via service mesh or LB to green, then cutover.
- In-place (minor patch): for low-risk patches and infra config that is compatible. Always run pre-sync health checks.

Release Checklist (pre-merge to main)
- CI: image built, signed, SBOM attached (if required).
- Tests: unit + smoke + infra integration tests passed.
- PR: values updated with digest + signed metadata.
- Approvals: security review (image policy), SRE readout if change touches runtime configs.
- Canary plan: rollout window, observability dashboard links, SLOs and rollback thresholds.
- Terraform: plan approved for infra changes, state backups validated.

Sync / Deployment Runbook (operator steps)
- Day 0: validate git branch state and that ArgoCD healthy (argocd health).
- Trigger: merge release PR to main branch (or tag). ArgoCD picks up or manual sync triggered.
- Validate: watch ArgoCD App health, check image verifier logs, confirm Pod readiness.
- Observability: correlate new pods with dashboard graphs, verify no CPU/memory anomalies and no spike in errors.
- Rollback: if failure criteria met, revert values commit (or set image back to previous digest) and sync. If stateful, follow data-restore runbook.

Rollback Guidance
- Application-level fast rollback: revert commit and let ArgoCD sync. Document the previous digest in the PR description to speed revert.
- Database/schema changes: require pre-migration toggle or backward-compatible migrations. Strongly prefer expand/contract. If not, treat as failover incident and escalate.

Troubleshooting Notes
- Verified images failing at pull time: check registry ACLs, cosign verification errors, and customer firewall rules.
- ArgoCD stuck sync: check argocd-repo-server logs for git fetch errors, repo credentials, chart repo access.
- Helm template failures: run helm template locally against the values file and the same chart digest.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide default policy when image-verifier is unavailable for 10+ minutes: block vs allow with manual approval.
- Formalize SBOM requirement per customer risk profile.
- Automate terraform plan approval gating into deployment PRs.

Appendix: Quick commands
- Validate helm template: helm template ./charts/component -f values/prod/component.yaml --set image.digest=sha256:...
- Cosign verify: cosign verify --key <kms-uri-or-pubkey> repo/image@sha256:...
- ArgoCD app sync: argocd app sync <app-name> --grpc-web
- Terraform plan: terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars

References
- Internal: Confluence: Private Deployments Home, Jira PD backlog (PD-298).
- External: cosign docs, ArgoCD app-of-apps pattern guide.

Notes to self:
- Save an extra paragraph with a minimal example repo structure (values, apps, charts) once we standardize the chart naming convention.
- Coordinate with security for key rotation schedule and a minimal verifier SLA.
